BEIJING, Nov 18 : Tencent Holdings reported third-quarter revenue growth of 8 per cent on Wednesday, slowing from 11 per cent in the previous quarter as gaming growth cooled, even as demand for artificial intelligence services lifted its cloud business. For the three months ending in September, the Chinese technology giant reported revenue of 207.34 billion yuan ($31.10 billion), falling short of analyst estimates of 210.77 billion yuan, according to LSEG data. Net profit rose 0.8 per cent from the period a year ago to 63.61 billion yuan ($9.54 billion), beating analyst expectations of 59.46 billion yuan. ($1 = 6.6659 Chinese yuan renminbi)

BANGKOK: Thailand will seek to cut a US Section 301 tariff to 10 per cent from 12.5 per cent after reaching agreement with Washington on the key terms of a reciprocal trade agreement, Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said on Wednesday (Nov 18). Thailand and the US signed a joint statement on the trade deal in Manila on Tuesday after agreeing on its key terms, she said in a statement. Thailand will seek to cut the US Section 301 tariff related to forced labour to 10 per cent from 12.5 per cent, in line with Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia. Legal teams are expected to take about two months to finalise the agreement before it is submitted to the Thai Cabinet.

The US is Thailand's largest export market, with exports worth about 2.37 trillion baht (US$70.2 billion) in 2025 and linked to around 1.25 million jobs. Thailand will open its market selectively, with quotas, import limits and other safeguards available to protect sensitive domestic industries. Fresh US restrictions on advanced chip exports affect about 0.7 per cent of Thailand's total chip imports and authorities see no broad impact so far, Suphajee said. Thailand will seek US clarification on the rules, help businesses prepare and work to prevent circumvention, the commerce ministry said in a separate statement.

FAST

KUALA LUMPUR: The global artificial intelligence boom will continue to drive Malaysia’s economy next year, the central bank said on Wednesday, downplaying risks from a potential sector slowdown and tighter scrutiny on data centres. Economic growth surpassed expectations in the third quarter, with gross domestic product rising 5.5 per cent from a year earlier, faster than 5.3 per cent expansions forecast by both a Reuters poll and the government's advance estimates. In September, growth accelerated 6.9 per cent, data from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Statistics Department showed. Malaysia's economic performance in the third quarter was underpinned by strong domestic demand, higher investment activities and robust tech exports, according to the data. "Looking ahead, the Malaysian economy is well positioned to build on this momentum in 2027, supported by strong fundamentals and positive outcomes from our structural reform," BNM Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said, adding that growth was likely to top 5 per cent this year.

The government raised its 2026 growth projections in October, and now expects the economy to expand close to the upper end of a 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent forecast range. It expects growth of between 4.2 per cent and 5.2 per cent in 2027. DATA CENTRE INVESTMENTS TO REMAIN 'STRONG' Malaysia has benefited from the AI boom, which has boosted exports of its semiconductors and other tech goods. Net exports rose 5.7 per cent from a year earlier, with shipments of electrical and electronic goods jumping 66.9 per cent, according to Wednesday's data. The country has also attracted billions of dollars in data centre investments, though analysts have warned that growth in the sector could slow following US curbs this week aimed at restricting China's access to advanced AI chips. Abdul Ghaffour said it was too early to assess the impact of the latest restrictions but said data centre investments in Malaysia were expected to remain strong until 2030, based on estimates of ongoing and planned projects. Out of 120 data centre companies, just 13 per cent were Chinese firms, with the rest from the US, Australia, Canada and Malaysia, he said. "It's very well diversified ... while there may be some reaction to (the latest curbs), we believe underlying demand is still strong," he said. While financial market volatility may weigh on AI investments, accelerated AI adoption could boost exports, Abdul Ghaffour said, adding that the tech upcycle will likely "be sustained until next year, although at a more moderate level." BNM SEES 'SPACE' TO MOVE ON RATES BNM kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged for the eighth straight meeting earlier this month. Economists, however, expect the central bank to raise the rate in the first quarter of 2027 amid a resilient economy and rising price pressures. Abdul Ghaffour said headline inflation was expected to edge higher - coming in between 1.5 per cent and 2.5 per cent in 2026 and 1.8 per cent to 2.8 per cent in 2027 - but remain relatively contained. He declined to comment on whether the central bank would hike rates, saying BNM would monitor whether price pressures were building widely and consistently. "If it happens, we have the space, we can be decisive in terms of our actions," he said. Bank Muamalat Malaysia chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Wednesday's data and the current outlook supported the case for a rate increase in 2027. "We foresee the Malaysian economy remaining on a respectable growth trajectory in 2026 and 2027, with the balance of risks fairly even," he said.

Source: Reuters/ec

FAST

LONDON, Nov 18 : Oil prices fell on Wednesday after an increase in US crude and fuel inventories, though losses were curbed by ongoing US-Iran fighting and attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.  Brent crude futures fell $1.15, or 1.2 per cent, to $91.99 a barrel by 0920 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures declined $1.67, or 2 per cent, to $84.34. Both contracts are on track for a 20 per cent decline this month on rising exports from the Middle East, underlined by plummeting shipping rates. The price spread between Brent and WTI has also widened in recent sessions, with WTI logging steeper declines during trading on Wednesday. The prompt Brent/WTI spread was hovering at a more than two-week high, LSEG data showed.

"WTI arbitrage trades have been shut to Asia and North West Europe, thus WTI correcting more than Brent is the expected price movement to allow the arbitrage window to open again," said June Goh at Sparta Commodities. This is particularly so with crude stocks building in the US Gulf Coast, Goh added. US crude stocks rose by 5.28 million barrels in the week to November 13, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Gasoline stocks rose by 5.12 million barrels and distillate inventories by 351,000 barrels. But continued US-Iran conflict and ongoing risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz kept price declines in check. Bahrain's defence force said on Wednesday that it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Both oil benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday as attacks on ships in the Middle East intensified, even as talks continued between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.  The United Arab Emirates' ADNOC L&S said on Wednesday that one crew member was missing and 11 injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. Iranian drones attacked a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday and the US retaliated with strikes on a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island. An LPG tanker was also struck by a projectile off the coast of Oman on Monday, leading its crew to evacuate the ship.  "Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalisation of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions," LSEG analysts said on Tuesday. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday that they had launched five drones towards two pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which it has used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 18 : Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Wednesday the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2 per cent target. Speaking in parliament, Ueda said it was important to see underlying inflation anchored around 2 per cent over time and conduct monetary policy appropriately to ensure that this could be achieved. "Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary easing in line with developments in the economy, prices and financial conditions," Ueda said. The BOJ kept interest rates steady at 1.25 per cent at its October 30 meeting but declared victory in its 14-year battle to hit its price target and stressed its policy had entered a new phase focused on avoiding an inflation overshoot, reinforcing its hawkish bias.

Once the details of the measure are finalised, the central bank will assess its impact on underlying inflation and reflect that analysis in future policy decisions, he added. Asked about the possibility of emergency bond-buying operations, Ueda said the BOJ would make a comprehensive assessment based on conditions at the time, including whether serious disruptions to market functioning had emerged and required a policy response. He also cautioned against using such operations to contain long-term yields, saying the move could prove counterproductive if markets perceive the BOJ as helping finance government spending. "In that case, long-term interest rates could become even more volatile," he said.

TOKYO, Nov 18 : The dollar held steady near a 19-month high on Wednesday as US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for interest rate hikes. The yen held its ground after Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated the need to tighten policy further. The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low ahead of a key jobs report on Thursday. Data on Tuesday showed US retail sales increased moderately in October, reinforcing expectations for a rate hike next month. Attention turns to US housing starts data due later on Wednesday as well as a series of Fed speakers, all ahead of the Thursday release of minutes of the central bank's meeting last month, when it held rates steady. "Overall, the report reinforces our view that further interest rate hikes from the Fed are warranted in order to counter demand-pull inflation," Henry Russell, a London-based economist for ANZ, said about the US sales data. "The strength of domestic demand in the US, in our view, warrants a decisive monetary policy response from the Fed."

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.06 per cent to 103.67. It touched 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. The euro was down 0.14 per cent at $1.0982, while the yen edged up 0.08 per cent to 159.25 per dollar. Sterling lost 0.13 per cent to $1.3191. In addition to a 0.2 per cent rise in retail sales that matched expectations, import prices climbed 1.1 per cent in October compared with expectations for a 0.7 per cent increase. More US data is expected with the Census Bureau due to report housing starts data for October. Analysts are projecting an increase to 1.245 million from 1.221 million in September, while building permits likely decreased. New York Fed President John Williams is expected to speak again following comments on Tuesday when he said the Fed will likely need to raise interest rates further to contend with inflation. Fed Board Governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari are also expected to speak at separate events.  Traders are pricing in a 95.7 per cent chance that the Fed will raise its key rate by 25 basis points (bps) in December, the CME FedWatch tool showed. The odds of a 50-bp increase have fallen to 4.3 per cent, from 13.5 per cent a month ago. "All Fed speakers are saying that the Fed should raise rates in an incremental way," said Tapas Strickland, chief market strategist at Moomoo ANZ, on a podcast. "The reduction in the probability of a supersized move has resulted in a bit more stability re-emerging in markets." Markets got a measure of relief after Nvidia reported after the bell that third-quarter revenue doubled and forecast higher-than-estimated sales for the fourth quarter, boosting shares in Asia. The next major test of sentiment will be the market debut of AI bellwether Anthropic on Thursday. Japanese data on Wednesday showed exports rose to a record monthly value in October on strong semiconductor-related demand. Also in Tokyo, BOJ Governor Ueda said the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2 per cent target. The Australian dollar sank 0.18 per cent versus the greenback to $0.6719 and earlier touched $0.6718, its lowest point since January 19. Data on Wednesday showed a surprise jump in Australian wages, but labour figures on Thursday are considered more crucial to determining if the central bank will need to hike rates again. The New Zealand dollar slid 0.07 per cent to $0.5488, approaching its 19-month low hit on Tuesday.

Source: Reuters

SAN FRANCISCO: Alphabet's Waymo has halted operations of its robotaxis on US freeways, it said on Tuesday (Nov 17), after a California regulator barred its vehicles from freeways in the state. The suspension is a setback for Waymo, which has been pushing for rapid expansion in the US and other countries after years of slow and steady growth, and comes as competitors such as Tesla and Amazon's Zoox make inroads into the robotaxi industry. The California ban, which took effect last week, is a result of a series of incidents where Waymo robotaxis entered active construction zones, the California Department of Motor Vehicles said in a statement on Tuesday. "The Department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety," it said.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 17 : Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has the ability to nominate two directors to the Nvidia board ahead of the company's annual shareholder meeting and vote, according to company proxy and corporate filings, giving the co-founder a route to future influence on the company. Chip industry executives, investors and customers are scrutinizing Nvidia closely to understand what role Huang will play in the company after he resigned as CEO last week. The ability to nominate directors, who choose leadership and provide oversight, could be a powerful tool in influencing the future of the AI chip leader. Any Nvidia shareholder or group of shareholders that owns more than 3 per cent of the voting power for at least three years is entitled to nominate directors who will be included in the company's proxy materials and vote at its annual meeting, which typically takes place in June. Huang and entities tied to him have owned more than 3 per cent of Nvidia's shares for more than three years, according to data from LSEG. He currently owns roughly 3.5 per cent of the company.

Huang would be free to nominate anyone who would qualify as an independent member of the board. The candidates would go on Nvidia's proxy ballot. Nominating board members would not guarantee Huang's allies seats on the company board; shareholders would need to vote to approve potential candidates. Nvidia may also leave a nominee out if the person has violated the company's bylaws and charter. FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE INVESTIGATION Nvidia's board said on November 8 that it initiated an investigation in light of recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Reuters could not determine if Huang's conduct broke the company's bylaws or charter. Nvidia and a representative for Huang did not respond to a request for comment. Since Huang resigned from Nvidia last week in the wake of his extramarital affairs, executives such as Elon Musk, employees, investors and US President Donald Trump have advocated for his return to the top job at the chip designer. The board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday. Huang released a statement on Tuesday and said he "would be honored" to return as CEO if the board decided such a move would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees. On Tuesday after the market close, Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates, giving investors some relief after the uncertainty caused by Huang's exit.

WASHINGTON, Nov 17 : The highly classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for its internal communications experienced a "temporary degradation" during scheduled maintenance, the agency said Tuesday. "While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues," the NSA said. CNN, which first reported on the outage, said that it affected NSANet, which allows employees to share classified information internally.  Reuters could not independently determine the extent or the length of the outage.

The incident comes amid increased concern over a series of tech problems, notably faults that snarled US air traffic and triggered a Microsoft email blackout late last week. US President Donald Trump on Tuesday played down the disruptions, saying such problems were inevitable. "Things like that happen," Trump told reporters in Manila when asked about the outages. "It's fine."

Source: Reuters
